name: Shilin Night Market
description: Shilin Night Market is one of the largest night markets in Taipei City. It is centered on the Yangming Theater and Cicheng Palace and includes lively streets such as Wenlin Road, Dadong Road, and Danan Road. The Shilin Market was built as early as 1910. It is famous at home and abroad for its various traditional snacks. Many tourists come here because of its various traditional snacks, such as pancakes, stone hot pot, and Shilin sausages. It has become a gourmet landmark and everyone knows it.

name: Raohe Street Tourist Night Market
description: Raohe Street Night Market is located on Raohe Street between Section 4 of Bade Road and Fuyuan Street in Songshan District. It is 600 meters long and is one of the large tourist night markets in downtown Taipei. The area around Raohe Street and Songshan Station was formerly known as Xikou. Due to the deep water of the Keelung River, the area was easily accessible by boat. It became a transfer station for goods from Keelung and Yilan to Taipei City. At that time, merchants gathered and boats came to the city. It was so prosperous that the area was known as "Little Suzhou". Later, due to the siltation of the harbor river, fewer and fewer boats were parked. In addition, after the widening of Bade Road, Raohe Street became a secondary road, and commercial activities were greatly reduced. In order to improve the livelihood of local businesses, the government concentrated the licensed vendors under the Nansongshan Bridge on Raohe Street in 1987. It was planned to be 500 meters long and became the second tourist night market in Taipei City. The stalls are neat and tidy, with a wide variety of items including oyster noodles, beef noodles, ice cream stalls, etc. In addition to snacks, various daily necessities such as clothing and leather shoes are also of high quality and low price. In addition, there are folk skills performances and local product exhibitions and sales.

name: Taipei Longshan Temple
description: Monga (now Wanhua) is the earliest developed place in Taipei City, and Taipei's first famous temple, Longshan Temple, is the center of local residents' beliefs, activities, gatherings and command. It is said that a man once hung the incense bag of Guanyin Bodhisattva on a big banyan tree, and it glowed at night. What's even more strange is that he responds to requests and is very effective. So believers built Longshan Temple in that place, which started in 1738 AD and was completed in 1740 AD. Over the past two hundred years, Longshan Temple has been built many times. The entire structure is in the shape of a complete "back", which is a very noble layout in traditional temple architecture. In the square, you can pay attention to the floor stones, the less neatly cut parts of which have ancient history.

name: National Palace Museum
description: The cultural relics and treasures collected by the National Palace Museum are world-famous cultural assets. From the collection of emperors to the collection of the National Palace Museum, which is shared by all the people, the collection of the National Palace Museum has been inherited in an orderly manner. The age of its collection almost covers the entire uninterrupted history of Chinese culture for more than 5,000 years, which is unique in the history of world civilization. Most of the more than 600,000 collections in the museum were collected by the Chinese royal family in the past, and the royal family's collection began in the Song Dynasty more than 1,000 years ago.

name: Dihua Street-New Year Goods Street
description: The commonly known Dihua Street, which has always been famous throughout Taiwan for its New Year shopping, actually refers to the section of Dihua Street south of the Taipei Bridge. In terms of spatial location, Dihua Street is part of Dadaocheng (now Datong District). The first store to appear on Dihua Street was in 1851 AD. Two years later, the Tongan people of Quanzhou in the Menga area built shops one after another on Dihua Street, forming "Middle Street". During the Japanese colonial period, the main products were groceries and tea products from the north and south. Later, the rice industry, cloth, and traditional Chinese medicine also gradually took their place. Later, as the times evolved, the streetscape and the appearance of the houses changed greatly. From the simple southern Fujian-style shops to the complex and gorgeous Baroque decoration, they gradually evolved into today's style.

name: Xinbeitou Hot Spring Area
description: Beitou hot spring area generally refers to more than ten places including Geothermal Valley, Longfeng, Fenghuang, Hushanli and Xingyi Road. In a narrow sense, "Beitou Hot Spring Area" mainly refers to the area surrounding Zhongshan Road, Guangming Road, Xinmin Road, and Quanyuan Road surrounding "Beitou Park". The hot spring hotels here are larger in scale, most concentrated in number, and have the richest natural and cultural resources.

name: Ximending Shopping District
description: The place name of Ximending comes from the Japanese colonial period. At that time, most residents lived in Taipei City, and the Ximen area was their resting place. In 1896, the first theater "Tokyo Pavilion" was built here. In 1922, it was officially named "Ximending".

name: Shilin Official Residence
description: Shilin Official Residence is located on the southeast side of the intersection of Section 5 of Zhongshan North Road and Fulin Road in Shilin District. It was originally part of the Horticulture Management Office (formerly the Shilin Horticulture Experimental Branch). After the Nationalist Government moved to Taiwan, in the 39th year of the Republic of China (1950 AD), President Chiang Kai-shek's official residence was located here. Since then, the Shilin Official Residence has become a sacred, mysterious and inaccessible forbidden place in the eyes of Taipei citizens. After 46 years of strict protection, the trend of democracy made Shilin Official Residence officially open in the 85th year of the Republic of China (1996 AD), becoming another place for tourists to visit during holidays. The official residence is divided into an outer garden, an inner garden, and the main room from the outside to the inside. There is a greenhouse potted area in the outer garden (mainly cultivated orchids), and the rose garden next to it (mainly cultivated roses) is also full of flowers. The rose garden is in full bloom from March to May, and it is Mrs. Chiang's favorite rose garden. The official residence is full of birdsong and flowers, and the landscape is quiet and elegant.

name: National Chiang Kai-shek Memorial Hall
description: The designer of the Chiang Kai-shek Memorial Hall is Yang Zhuocheng, who designed the Grand Hotel. The original site of the memorial hall was the Army Headquarters, which was the largest military district in Taipei City at the time. The blue and white colors used in the memorial hall are the main colors on the national flag. The decoration of the sky dome at the top of the memorial hall is the 12 rays of the blue sky and the white sun. With the evolution of democracy and open-mindedness, the square in front of the memorial hall has become a meeting place for the democratic movement.

name: Huaxi Street Tourist Night Market
description: The Huaxi Street Tourist Night Market is located near Longshan Temple. It is the first tourist night market in Taiwan. It mainly sells a variety of mountain products, seafood and game snacks. It is one of the most popular attractions for tourists at home and abroad.

name: Taipei 101
description: About Taipei 101 TAIPEI 101 is located in the most elite area of ​​Taipei and is the largest engineering project in the history of the domestic construction industry. This project was mainly planned by Taipei Financial Tower Co., Ltd., a joint venture of 14 domestic companies, and professional teams at home and abroad. It was carefully designed by international architect Li Zuyuan. It transcended the design concept of a single volume and used the auspicious number "eight" (a homophone of "fa") as the design unit. Every eight floors is a structural unit, which are connected to each other and stacked layer by layer to form the whole. It forms a rhythmic beauty in appearance and creates a new style of international skyscrapers.

name: Taipei Martyrs' Shrine
description: The Martyrs' Shrine is located next to the Grand Hotel, leaning against the green hills and facing the Keelung River. Built in the 58th year of the Republic of China (1969 AD), it occupies a vast area. The main building is modeled after the Hall of Supreme Harmony in the Forbidden City in Beijing. It is majestic and majestic, symbolizing the fearless spirit of the martyrs. The more than 10,000 square meters of green grassland surrounding the Martyrs' Shrine, surrounded by mountains, creates a quiet and solemn atmosphere, which further highlights the solemnity of the building.

name: Dadaocheng
description: Dadaocheng was originally the residence of the Pingpu people. Due to fierce armed fighting between Wanhua (Mengga) and the An people, the tribesmen moved to Dadaocheng to settle down, and began to build shops and houses next to the Tamsui River in Dadaocheng. After the opening of Tamsui Port, Dadaocheng was established by Liu Mingchuan. Under its governance, it became the most prosperous material distribution center in Taipei City, with tea and cloth as the main trade transactions. At that time, Yanping North Road and Guide Street were the focus of commercial activities, making Dadaocheng's early history colorful and evocative.

name: Presidential Office Building
description: The Presidential Palace is located at No. 122, Section 1, Chongqing South Road, Zhongzheng District, Taipei City. The main gate faces Ketagalan Avenue, the front (eastward) is Chongqing South Road, the back (westward) is Boai Road, the north is Baoqing Road, and the south is Guiyang Street.

name: Fenfenpu-Garment Street
description: This is the center of Taipei's clothing wholesale industry. I believe everyone's first thought is "Fenfenpu". There are hundreds of wholesale stores clustered near Songshan Railway Station. The origin of its name is that during the Qing Dynasty, Wufenpu was the activity area of ​​the Taiwanese aboriginal Pingpu tribe. Later, five families, He, Zhou, Shen, Du, and Li, bought this land from the Pingpu tribe to cultivate it, and named the village Wufenpu. Taiwan's economic development over the past half century, from poverty to working day and night to prosperity, is just like the development history of Fenfenpu. People from the central and southern parts of the country who went north to make a living gathered in Fenfenpu. They simply processed and patched the leftover bits and pieces of unsalable fabrics from exported garments into underwear, children's clothing or rough work clothes for sale at roadside stalls and retail stores, gradually developing the name Wufenpu. Now, hundreds of garment manufacturers gather here, with goods sourced from all over Taiwan, and even imported from as far away as Hong Kong, Thailand, South Korea, Singapore and other regions. Cheap clothing attracts small businesses to wholesale and retail. Due to the wide variety of styles and popular cuts, many young people also come to shop, matching them to their liking to create eye-catching fashion styles. When the desire to shop arises, but the budget is insufficient or you don’t want to bleed a lot of money, the most suitable place is Wufenpu. It is worth mentioning that bargaining is also a common shopping phenomenon here, which is similar to the old people.

name: Guandu Palace
description: Guandu Temple was founded around 1712 AD to worship Mazu. It is the oldest Mazu temple in northern Taiwan. It was originally called Lingshan Temple and is located on the top of Lingshan Mountain. According to legend, in 1895 AD, three old banyan trees at the entrance of the temple died on the same night. Residents believed that Mazu might be warning them of a disaster. Sure enough, not long after, the Japanese army occupied Guandu and burned and killed everywhere. However, the residents were able to escape the disaster because they had taken precautions in advance. Guandu Palace has a long history. The dragon pillars, stone lions, wall carvings, etc. at the entrance of the palace are all very exquisite. Especially the door god is represented in relief, which has a very different charm from the ordinary painting method. Entering the hall, the caissons, brackets, beams and rafters on the top of the hall are rich in sculptures and paintings, which are very beautiful. The statue of Mazu, who has many legends, is sitting in the main niche with a kind expression, which forms a strong contrast with the appearance of her generals who are clairvoyant and have ears for the wind.

name: Daan Forest Park
description: Da'an Forest Park is located in the city center, bordered by Jianguo South Road to the east, Xinsheng South Road to the west, Heping East Road to the south, and Xinyi Road to the north. It was officially opened in the 83rd year of the Republic of China (1994 AD). The park is full of lush trees, well-organized shrubs, blooming flowers, chirping birds, and fragrant flowers. During a walk, you feel like you are in a beautiful forest.

name: Taipei City Blue Highway
description: Tamsui River and Keelung River in Taipei City have been blue waterways for freight or commuter ferries since ancient times. Now it has been transformed into a water sightseeing road carrying tourists.

name: Maokong Cable Car
description: Maokong is located in the Muzha area of ​​Wenshan District, Taipei City, on the upper reaches of Jingmei Creek and on the south bank of Nanjing Creek. It belongs to the Erge Mountain System on the southern edge of the Taipei Basin. It is the southernmost tip of Taipei City and adjacent to Xindian District, New Taipei City. Close to National Chengchi University and Guide Scenic Area. There are different opinions on the origin of the place name Maokong. The most common theory is that it comes from the special "pot hole" riverbed landscape. Due to the uneven hardness of the geology, the "pot hole" terrain of pits and holes was formed after being washed by the river. The local people called it "ㄋㄧㄠ ㄎㄤ". During the Japanese occupation, the name "Maokong" was recorded and passed down. The Tie Guanyin produced in Maokong is famous far and wide, and it has rich cultural history and natural ecological landscape. It is located on the outskirts of Taipei and the terrain is relatively high. The bamboo and cypress path, Huxue Suspension Bridge, camphor tree trail, etc. belong to the seventh section of the "Taipei Great Longitudinal Walk". It is a good place for urbanites, hikers and domestic and foreign tourists to go hiking in the mountains, drink tea, watch the stars and the moon, and overlook the city's night view.

name: Taipei Municipal Zoo
description: Taipei Municipal Zoo is located in Wenshan District, also known as Muzha Zoo, near National Chengchi University. It was officially opened on October 31, 1986, the 75th year of the Republic of China. The current total area of ​​the park is 165 hectares. The design of the park makes full use of the terrain and maintains the landscape and natural ecology.

name: Miramar Paradise
description: Located in Taipei City, the new-concept commercial facility "Miramar Park" is erected on the new land at the big bend of the Keelung River. It combines six years of planning by a well-known design, planning and investment team at home and abroad. It has two buildings, the main building and the Yangtze building.

name: National Museum of History
description: The National Museum of History is located in the Botanical Garden on Nanhai Road. Its architectural style is classical Chinese architecture.

name: Xinyi Business District
description: The Xinyi Planning District is an emerging commercial district and is currently the most iconic business district in Taipei. There are many department stores, hotels, and fashionable restaurants between Sections 4 and 5 of Xinyi Road. It is known as the most valuable area in Taipei, including Shin Kong Mitsukoshi Taipei Xinyi Plaza, Breeze Department Store, United Times Department Store, Village Roadshow Cinemas, Far Eastern Department Store, Grand Hyatt Hotel, etc., plus Taipei 101, this area has gradually replaced the East District as a new fashionable urban area.

name: Jianguo Holiday Flower Market and Jade Market
description: The Jianguo Holiday Flower Market and Jade Market are located between Xinyi Road and Jinan Road. The holiday is in the form of a market, with Renai Road as the boundary, the flower market to the south, and the Jade Market to the north. There are many kinds of flowers in the flower market, which are of high quality and low price; there are nearly a thousand jade stalls in the jade market, which can be said to be one of the largest jade markets in Asia, attracting tourists from Luoyi to visit and buy.

name: Xingtian Palace
description: Xingtian Temple, also known as the Enzhugong Temple, is dedicated to Emperor Guan Sheng (AD 162-219 AD), a famous warrior in Chinese history. Because he upheld his faith, he was revered as the Martial Saint; and because he was good at managing money, he was revered as the patron saint of business.

name: Flower Expo Park
description: The "2010 Taipei International Flower Expo" (Taipei Flower Expo for short) is Taiwan's first world-class expo to receive international authorization. It has achieved a record of 8.963,666 visitors in 171 days of operation. In order to continue the beautiful power of the Flower Expo, the Taipei City Government planned flower arrangements after the Flower Expo. The Expo Park integrates the three major parks of the original Flower Expo, Yuanshan, Art and Xinsheng, and organizes exhibitions and series of activities with themes such as cultural and creative, art, parent-child, diversified education, silver hair, happiness, LOHAS... to enhance citizens' literacy in culture, art, technology, environmental protection, ecology... and become a high-quality resting place.

name: Sisi South Village
description: Fourth Fourth South Village was a product of the Civil War between the Kuomintang and the Communist Party. It was also the first military dependent village in Taipei. It was called "Four Fourth South Village" because it was located south of the Fourth Fourth Arsenal. There is a bunker from that time in the park, which was specially preserved by the designer. Although it has lost its previous functions, it is a trace of the history of Sisi South Village. There are many exhibition halls in the park, and many private houses retain their appearance at that time. Many cultural and creative elements have been added to the park, and there are also many products for sale.

name: National Dr. Sun Yat-Sen Memorial Hall
description: ※ The museum will be undergoing construction work on the "City Hall and Surrounding Facilities Project" from February 26, 2020 to the fourth quarter of 2020, and will be closed to the public. The Zhongshan Cultural Park will remain open normally and will not be affected.

name: Zhinan Temple
description: The name of the Guanzhi Temple comes from the meaning of "Lord Lu En lives in the South Palace in Heaven" and "A compass is necessary to help the world and save people". It mainly serves Lu Dongbin (Lord Lu En) and is commonly known as the "Xian Gong Temple". It has now become a temple of Confucianism, Taoism and Buddhism. It is considered one of the Taoist holy places in Taiwan and the main belief in the Guanzhi area.

name: Maokong Tea Garden
description: Maokong is located in the southwest of Getou Mountain in Muzha District, a suburb of Taipei. The word "Maokong" is related to the valley topography in the tea research center area. When the stream carries a large amount of sand and gravel over the years, a round or oval cave is formed on the stream bed. It is called "pot cave" in geology and "pot cave" in Hokkien. "Liaokang" (meaning a wrinkled pothole), it was not until the Japanese colonial era that it was renamed "Maokong" with a similar pronunciation; however, today's Maokong later developed into a very special tea tourism industry due to its proximity to the student activities area of National Chengchi University, and student nightlife promoted regional prosperity.

name: Bopiliao Old Street
description: Bopiliao Old Street is located on the south side of today's Wanhua Laosong Elementary School. The address is Lane 173, Kangding Road. The street houses on the north side of the old street are only separated from the Laosong Elementary School campus by a wall, while the street houses on the south side are close to Guangzhou Street. Laosong Elementary School, founded in 1896, is a century-old school with a long history. The north building of the campus building is designated as a municipal historic site, and the east and west buildings are designated as historical buildings. There is also a "Taipei City Native Education Center" next to Laosong Elementary School, where school children can visit and study.

name: Dalongdong Baoan Palace
description: Bao Bao Temple occupies a vast area and was built in 1805 AD. Due to the vast and arduous construction project, the required stones and timber had to be shipped from China, and the craftsmen were specially hired from the local area. Therefore, the entire project was constructed in stages and took 25 years to complete.

name: Beitou Cultural Heritage Museum
description: The Art Museum was built in the 1920s with exquisite workmanship. It is one of the largest single Japanese-style pure wooden buildings in Taiwan. During the Japanese colonial period, it was a Japanese officers' club and was once used by kamikaze troops. After World War II, it became the Ministry of Foreign Affairs' Jiashan Guest House. It is now privately owned and is a place where folk art antiques are exhibited.

name: Guandu Pier
description: Guandu, formerly known as Gandoumen, has become a port with dangerous terrain because it is backed by Guanyin Mountain and Datun Mountain and faces the Tamsui River. In the early years, the ancestors moved to northern Taiwan from the Guandu Wharf to cultivate land. Therefore, Guandu was developed very early. Later, due to sedimentation at the mouths of the two rivers (Keelung River and Tamsui River), water transportation gradually declined.

name: Guandu Natural Park
description: Guandu Nature Park is located at the intersection of Tamsui River and Keelung River, a low-lying land in the southwest corner of Guandu Plain in the Taipei Basin. It is a famous waterbird viewing and swamp life observation area. Outside the embankment on the south side is a large swampland of Shuibizi mangroves. The Guandu Natural Park within the embankment covers a total area of ​​57 hectares. Due to the low terrain, water accumulated in many places, forming shallow water and mudflats, which gradually evolved into swamps and wetlands. In addition, some farmland was abandoned and waste soil was deposited to change some of the landforms. As a result, the plants in the park evolved into various communities such as aquatic, hygrophytic and xerophytic, providing a diverse living space for organisms. Every spring and autumn, thousands of waterbirds use it as an important supply station or wintering place for migrating south to north. In the 70th year of the Republic of China (1981 AD), with the promotion of bird watching activities, people gradually realized the value of nature and also felt that many environments had been destroyed. Many conservationists therefore promoted the creation of Guandu Natural Park. After seven mayors, Guandu Natural Park was officially opened in 2001.

name: Taipei Beitou-the elegant town of Sulfur Springs and Jade Dew
description: "Beitou" is recommended by the New York Times Travel website as Taiwan's hot spring paradise. It has rich natural resources and rich history and culture. It is a famous tourist destination in Taipei City. Its territory covers Beitou Hot Spring, Yangmingshan National Park, Guandu Scenic Area, etc.

name: National Theater and Concert Hall
description: Taiwan's first national-level cultural park, Liangtingyuan, was completed in 1987. It is the most professional theater for performing arts in Taiwan and an important tourist landmark in Taipei. The two main buildings combine the style of a Chinese palace, with yellow tile cornices and red columns and colorful arches. They are elegant and spectacular, creating an elegant and artistic living space.

name: Songshan Cultural and Creative Park
description: Songshan Cultural and Creative Park, located in Xinyi District, Taipei City, covers an area of ​​6.6 hectares. It was formerly known as the "Taiwan Governor's Office Monopoly Songshan Tobacco Factory" built in 1937. It was later taken over by the Taiwan Tobacco and Liquor Monopoly Bureau and renamed "Taiwan Tobacco and Liquor Monopoly Songshan Tobacco Factory". It is the first modern cigarette factory in Taiwan. It produces cigarettes and cigars and created considerable economic output for Taiwan at the time. In 1998, due to factors such as declining demand, production was stopped and the Taipei Tobacco Factory was moved. Designated as the 99th municipal historic site by the Taipei City Government in 2021, it was transformed into Songshan Cultural and Creative Park and officially opened to the public on November 15, 2011. Positioned as the "Taipei City Original Base", it combines the revitalization of historical buildings and the support of cultural and creative industries, and has become an important core of Taipei City's cultural and creative industries, gathering art, Design and cultural creativity exhibitions, with strategies such as "cross-border experiments", "creative showcases" and "creator factories", as well as self-organized activities such as the "Songshan Cultural and Creative School Festival", "Summer Relaxation" and "Original Base Festival", have become an internationally competitive cultural life site and opened up more possibilities for Taiwan's cultural and creative industry. Songshan Cultural and Creative Park retains the Japanese Secession architectural style, including: city-designated historic sites (office building, warehouses 1-5, cigarette factory, boiler room), historical buildings (inspection

name: Qingshuiyan Patriarch Temple
description: Menga Qingshuiyan, also known as the "Ancestral Temple", was built in 1787 AD. Together with Menga Longshan Temple and Dalongdong Baoan Temple, it is also known as the "Three Major Temple Gates in Taipei". The Qingshui Patriarch Chen Zhaoying who is the main worshiper was an immigrant from Anxi, Fujian Province. There are seven statues in total, among which the Penglai Patriarch is the most spiritual, also known as the "Luubi Patriarch". According to legend, when natural disasters occur, the ancestor's nose will fall off on its own to warn believers that it will not recover until the disaster passes.

name: Taipei Botanical Garden
description: Since its establishment in 1921, the Botanical Garden has been a part of the memories of many Taipei people. Stopping here to take a break in your free time, whether it is the lotus flowers in summer or the fallen leaves in winter, is a fond memory for many people. The botanical garden is affiliated to the Forestry Experimental Institute of the Ministry of Agriculture. On January 22, 1921, the forestry experimental site was officially designated as a botanical garden. By around 1930, 1,120 species of plants had been planted in the park, most of which were imported from abroad, making great contributions to academic and natural science education. However, during World War II, all the trees in the park were lost. After World War II, the park was reorganized and various foreign tree species were actively introduced for planting. So far, the types of buildings and plants in the park have far exceeded those in the past, with more than a thousand species of plants collected.

name: Qingshan Palace
description: It was established in 1854 AD and is dedicated to King Ling'an, also known as King Qingshan.

name: Songshan Ciyou Palace
description: Ciyou Palace was built in 1753 AD and was the origin of the development of Songshan area. Songshan was once called Xikou. The plaque on the main entrance of Songshan Ciyou Palace reads "Xikou Ciyou Palace". A long time ago, there was a monk who traveled around with the golden body of Meizhou Mazu to beg for alms. One day he came to Xikou. There were many people in the local area who were from the same hometown as him. In addition, people believed in Mazu, so everyone donated money together to build a Mazu palace. After more than ten years of raising funds, construction finally started in 1753 and was completed in 1757.

name: National Taiwan Science Education Center
description: Taiwan Science Education Center takes science out of the laboratory and integrates it naturally into daily life, allowing you to easily discover the fun of science in life. It not only answers every curiosity and doubt about "why", but also opens up the infinite horizons of science and takes you into the mysterious world of science in a simple and profound way. In the life science and natural science exhibition rooms on the third and fourth floors, you can see the mysteries of human evolution and heredity and genes. The fifth and sixth floors showcase a world of scientific games composed of various "strength and motion" experience devices. There are also various interesting exhibitions and installations on other floors.

name: Taipei Confucius Temple
description: Walk through Dalong Street and come to the Confucius Temple. The Confucius Temple is dedicated to worshiping the greatest teacher in China, Confucius, the sage of Dacheng, as well as the sages and Confucian scholars of the past dynasties. Since Confucius advocated simplicity, the architecture of the Confucius Temple is relatively simple and plain. Unlike other temples that have gorgeous decorations, and there are no stone lions at the door. The Confucius Temple is dominated by the Dacheng Hall. Standing outside the Dacheng Hall, you can see a pair of cylinders on the roof in the middle, called "Sutra Storage Tubes." In ancient Chinese history, Qin Shihuang implemented a policy of obscuring the people in order to facilitate his rule. He burned books and killed scholars. At that time, in order to preserve the books, the scholars built a chimney-like library on the roof and hid the books there to avoid the fate of being burned. Therefore, the Confucius Temple also built a scripture tube to express admiration for the book-loving spirit of the scholars at that time. At the same time, on the roof in front, there is a carving of an owl. The owl is an unfilial and cruel bird, but Confucius also educated it. Therefore, the owl sculpture represents Confucius's spirit of "teaching without discrimination".

name: Taipei Arena
description: The Arena is the first international large-scale comprehensive stadium in Taiwan. It is divided into a main hall and an auxiliary hall. The main hall is a multi-purpose gymnasium that can be used for multiple sports competitions, exhibitions, art performances, concerts, gatherings and other large-scale activities. It has 15,000 spectator seats and has 48 VIP boxes, the first of its kind in China. The auxiliary hall has an 800-seat ice rink and a health and leisure center. It is planned to have a gym, dance studio and squash court.

name: Taipei 228 Peace Park
description: 228 Peace Park is located at the bottom of Qianguan Road, Taipei Station. It was originally named Taipei Park, also known as New Park. Built in 1899, it is the oldest park in Taipei City. In the 34th year of the Republic of China (1945 AD), the Nationalist Government took over Taiwan after World War II, and the people of Taiwan were delighted. However, a series of inappropriate measures taken by the Nationalist Government in Taiwan later led to public resentment, including economic monopoly and monopoly, corruption in political style, decline in people's livelihood, and the domination of the military and police. In addition, cultural differences have deepened the gap between people from this province and those from other provinces. Finally, on the night of February 27, the 36th year of the Republic of China (1947 AD), due to the anti-smuggling operation, people were dissatisfied with the killing of people by anti-smuggling agents and surrounded the military police unit, but they were shot by soldiers. On February 28, people gathered in Taipei Park (today’s 228 Peace Park), and then occupied the Taiwan Broadcasting Station (today’s Taipei 228 Memorial Hall) to broadcast to the entire Taiwan. The chaos gradually spread across Taiwan, and the demand for punishment of the perpetrators became a political protest. The Nationalist Government mobilized troops to suppress the uprising, and in addition to carrying out forceful sweeps, they also carried out clearing out the countryside after the chaos subsided. Qingxiang's execution methods were extreme, either by incriminating others or using excuses to retaliate, putting everyone in the province at risk. In order to heal the scars of historical events, in the 85th year of the Republic of China (AD

name: National Taiwan Museum
description: The National Taiwan Museum was established in 1908 and is the oldest museum in Taiwan. At that time, the Japanese government established the "Taiwan Governor's Palace Museum" in 1908 to commemorate the opening of the North-South Railway in Taiwan. The new building was opened in 228 Peace Park (formerly known as Taipei New Park) in 1915. The designer was Japanese architect Ichiro Nomura. The architectural style imitated the Doric style of ancient Greece during the Renaissance. Its majestic architectural form and beautiful classical sculpture craftsmanship have always been regarded as a rare architectural treasure in modern Taiwan.

name: Xuehai Academy
description: Xuehai Academy, formerly known as Wenhai Academy, has now become the Gao family ancestral hall. The ancestral hall is a traditional Chinese family gathering place for discussion. The Chinese family concept is still very strong today, and the ancestral hall plays a very important role. The front hall is the lecture hall in the past, the back hall is the sacrificial hall, and the left and right wing rooms are the school buildings. Academy education is an important part of traditional Chinese education and the predecessor of today's school education. It has the functions of teaching, worship, and residence. Both students and teachers live in the academy. The teaching content focuses on the cultivation of personality rather than just the teaching of specialized knowledge, which is very different from the modern fine-grained education.

name: Xinyi District
description: Xinyi District, the most unique tourist city in Taiwan, is a city built with the dream blueprint of the Xinyi Project. It is also a fashionable city in Taiwan that represents fashion trends, dream creation, and is full of vitality. With convenient intercity transfer stations, boutique department stores with the most international brands in Taiwan, the largest Eslite bookstore in Taiwan, the most internationally renowned Taipei 101 building, the reconstructed April 4th South Village, the flagship Songshan Cultural and Creative Park, internationally renowned Michelin-starred restaurants, charming architectural landscapes and installations created by international masters, and the most HIGH New Year's Eve party in Taiwan, Xinyi District exudes the most dazzling starry charm.

name: Zhishan Cultural Ecological Green Park
description: Zhishan Cultural and Ecological Green Park is located opposite Yang-Ming Hospital. In addition to natural scenery such as aquatic ponds and century-old liquidambar trees, the Zhishan Rock Exhibition Hall has a 360° panoramic model on the first floor to describe the development and geographical relationship between Zhishan Rock and the surrounding Taipei City. It also has detailed literature to introduce the human history and natural ecology of Zhishan Rock.

name: Neidouxi Nature Center Medicinal Plant Garden
description: In order to promote the concept of forest ecological conservation and enhance the understanding and cherishment of wild plants, the Industrial Development Bureau of the Taipei City Government has specially established a 0.3-hectare "Forest Medicinal Botanical Garden" in Inner Shuangxi Forest Nature Park. There are six areas planned in the park, namely the "Twelve Zodiac Medicinal Plants Area" named after the zodiac animals, and the "Five Elements Medicinal Plants Area" named after the five elements. These two areas focus on the "name" and are convenient for people to learn in an interesting way; the "Inner Shuangxi Native Medicinal Plants Area" introduces the local wild medicinal plants in the park; "Baicao Tea Medicinal Plants" The "Plant Area" captures the wisdom of ancestors in their daily lives. The raw materials of Baicao Tea are introduced here. The "Poisonous Plant Area" introduces common poisonous plants to remind the public not to abuse them. In addition, many fruit trees are planted and planned as the "Fruit Tree Health Medicinal Plant Area" to remind the public that fruits are not only delicious, but also have special curative effects.

name: Ximen Red House
description: The Ximen Red Building was completed in 1908. It was originally the first officially built public market in Taiwan, and it is also the oldest and most complete historical market building currently preserved. It was designed by Juro Kondo, a Japanese architect who worked in the Maintenance Department of the Taiwan Governor's Office and was good at Western architectural styles. The young and bold creativity used the "Bagua shape", which means gathering from all directions, as the entrance to the market, and the "Cross shape" as the main feature of the market. This is not only unprecedented, but also the first in the history of Eastern and Western architecture. Today, what everyone calls the Octagonal Tower and the Cross Tower, together with the north and south squares on both sides, are collectively known as the "Ximen Red Tower".

name: Linantai Ancient House Folk Culture Museum
description: The Lin Antai Ancient House located in Binjiang Park is a traditional Chinese courtyard house with rigorous layout and elegant carvings. It is a rare ancient building in northern Taiwan that has been completely preserved. Lin Yao, the founder of the Lin family, crossed the sea from Anxi to Taiwan in 1754. His son Lin Hui was engaged in trading business in Menga. The shop was named Rongtai Hao. Because of his skillful management, he made a lot of money. Therefore, in 1783, he built a house near the current Siwei Road and named it "Antai". Lin Antai Ancient House has a history of more than 160 years. When Lin Hui first built it, it was just a house with five rooms. Later, the left and right wing rooms and the entrance hall were added one after another to become a courtyard. In the late Qing Dynasty, two outer wing rooms and a study room were added to form the current layout of two rooms with four rooms. It is the most complete ancient house building in Taipei City.

name: Huashan 1914 Cultural and Creative Industry Park
description: Huashan 1914 Cultural and Creative Industrial Park was formerly a Taipei Winery. The buildings were built by the Japanese in 1914. In the early days, it was a factory for Japanese sake production, and later it was a Taipei Winery. After the Taipei Winery was relocated in 1987, Huashan's role as a winery industry came to an end. The entire factory is a museum of industrial construction technology. After the Republic of China in 1999, it gradually became a diversified arts and cultural exhibition and performance area. It is a creative venue used by the art and literary circles, groups and individuals. There are also many restaurants, art galleries, cultural and creative shops and performance venues in the park. It also provides rental services for various performance venues. It is the flagship base of Taiwan's cultural and creative industries.

name: Taipei Xiahai City God Temple
description: In 1853 AD, there was a fierce fight among immigrants from Monga. The people of Tong'an County failed, so they snatched the golden statue of the Xiahai City God in the flames and retreated to Dadaocheng. In 1859, they built the Xiahai City God Temple, which became the center of faith in Dadaocheng.

name: Bishanyan Kaizhang Shengwang Temple
description: Bishan Rock is located on Bishan Mountain in Neihu. The temple is dedicated to Chen Yuanguang, the national hero of the founding of Fujian, and his two generals Li Boyao and Ma Ren. Chen Yuanguang opened up the Zhangzhou area in Fujian Province at the end of the Tang Dynasty. He was regarded as the patron saint of Zhangzhou people and was honored as the "King of Kai Zhang". Bishanyan is one of the largest Kaizhang Shengwang temples in Taiwan and is very popular. Legend has it that when Huang, a man from Zhangzhou Prefecture, crossed the sea to Taiwan with his family to cultivate land, he saw that this place was a rare and auspicious place, so he hung the incense stick with him in the cave to worship before leaving. Later, bandits were rampant in the lower part of the mountain. They were robbing homes and houses, making the people there miserable. In 1751 AD, when the bandits were about to attack the top, they suddenly saw sharp lights and war drums beating on the top of the mountain. It turned out that the sacred incense stone hung at that time was divided into three parts. The middle piece was the Holy King, and the stones on both sides were Generals Li and Ma. The surrounding stones rolled down the mountain, causing the bandits to abandon their weapons and flee. After hearing the news, nearby residents came to worship here. As expected, the gods blessed him, so they built a small stone temple. Later, due to the increasing number of pilgrims, the original small stone temple was not enough for a large number of pilgrims to worship, so a new main temple was built on the original site. Then there were several natural disasters. After several renovations, with the efforts of many local people, believers and temple management committee members, it was expanded to the present day.

name: Yangming Study
description: Yangming Bookstore was originally a hot spring villa area for Japan's leading elites during the Japanese colonial period. President Chiang Kai-shek believed that the scenery here was beautiful and excellent, so he built the "Zhongxing Hotel" here, the predecessor of Yangming Bookstore, to receive foreign guests, host meetings and escape from the summer heat. Later, Yangmingshan Villa and Zhongshan Tower were built nearby. Many government officials often held meetings here, making Yangmingshan the decision-making center of the national government.

name: Taipei Municipal Astronomy Science Education Center
description: In 1938, in order to commemorate the 40th anniversary of its founding, "Taiwan Daily News" donated its 4-inch refractor equatorial telescope and dome observation platform built on the roof of the public hall to the Taipei City Hall. In the 34th year of the Republic of China (1945 AD), the Public Hall was taken over by the city government and was renamed Zhongshan Hall. This was the earliest predecessor of the Taipei Municipal Astronomy Science Education Center. Afterwards, human culture entered the space age, and society had a strong demand for astronomical knowledge. Because the light pollution near Zhongshan Hall was severe at night, it was not suitable for observation work. Therefore, after planning, it was decided to locate the observatory in the Yuanshan Scenic Area. It was opened in 1963, and a planetarium was built in 1978. Later, due to the rapid increase in the population of Taipei City, the original observatory was too small to be used. So preparations began for the planetarium now located on Jihe Road.

name: National History Museum
description: The National History Museum is located on Changsha Street behind the Presidential Palace. The building is a city-designated historic site that combines Western classical and modern styles. In its early days, it was the Communications Department of the Transportation Bureau of the Taiwan Governor-General during the Japanese occupation. In October 2010, the "President and Vice President Cultural Relics Exhibition" was launched, displaying themes and cultural relics related to the president and vice president, as well as diplomatic gifts from various countries around the world. In addition to scheduled tours and group reservation tours, it also organizes related promotion and education events, including a series of lectures, special lectures on cultural relics, etc.; it also provides digitized archives of the collection for retrieval and application by all walks of life.

name: Taipei Museum of Contemporary Art
description: Taipei Museum of Contemporary Art is located on Chang'an West Road in Taipei. It was established after the revitalization and reuse of historical sites. Under the long-term attention of the domestic art circle, it was officially opened in May of the Republic of China 90 (2001 AD). It is also the first art museum in Taiwan with the purpose of promoting contemporary art.

name: Tap Water Park - Tap Water Museum
description: As early as the Qing Dynasty leader Liu Mingchuan in Taiwan, deep wells were dug for water supply in Taipei's Beimen Street (today's Hengyang Road), Shifang Street (today's Boai Road), Ximen Street and other places, marking the beginning of Taipei's public water supply.

name: Taipei Puppet Theater
description: The Taipei Puppet Theater mainly holds puppet exhibitions, performances, teaching and other activities. You can also purchase puppet artworks.

name: Taipei Fine Arts Museum
description: The Taipei Fine Arts Museum was officially opened on December 24, 1983. Located in Yuanshan, North District, Taipei City, it covers an area of ​​20,442 square meters and has 11,741 square meters of graphic display space. As Taiwan's first modern art museum, the Taipei Fine Arts Museum has high ideals and goals since its planning. Functionally, it organizes and curates contemporary art exhibitions, collects and archives representative works of Taiwan's art development, studies art academics, promotes art education, and promotes international exchanges, in order to internally integrate citizens' lives with the museum, and externally promote Taiwan's art development to keep pace with international art trends.

name: Shunyi Taiwan Aboriginal Museum
description: It was officially opened in June 1994 as an anthropology museum. The founder, Mr. Lin Qingfu, loved Taiwan’s local art and continuously invested in the collection, research and promotion of aboriginal cultural relics, hoping to contribute to aboriginal culture. It has now accumulated nearly a thousand cultural relics. In the future, for the needs of display, education, research and preservation, we will continue to collect or copy relevant cultural relics and conduct research work. It is one of the few museums in China that is funded by enterprises and displays a single feature.

name: Dajia Pier
description: Dajia Wharf is located on the left bank of the Keelung River in Yuanshan. Yuanshan, formerly known as Yuanzi Mountain, is the leading place on the Dalongdong terrain. Because the Keelung River flows through it, it used to be a lake and swamp area where sea water flows in and out. The excavation of the Yuanshan ruins and shell mounds proves the location where the ancestors lived at that time. The Sword Pond area, which is close to the Grand Mountain Hotel, was named after Zheng Chenggong, the country's surname, inserted his sword into the pond to draw water. During the Japanese colonial period, the Japanese built the Taiwan Shrine and the shrine's outer garden on the site to the west of the Martyrs' Shrine next to the present-day Grand Mountain Hotel. This shows the importance of its geographical location.

name: National Taiwan Art Education Center
description: In order to promote social education institutions for art education and cultural construction, the central government specially established the Taiwan Art Education Center in Nanhai Academy. The central concept of the museum is based on the interaction between people and art. The biggest contribution of the Art Education Center is to promote the research, promotion and guidance of art education. The development of the museum's affairs is in line with educational standards and social needs. It also cooperates with education reform policies and meets the people's lifelong learning needs. It covers general art education in schools, social art education and professional art education, with the aim of popularizing the public's understanding, appreciation, participation and application of art and improving the quality of national life.

name: Yangmingshan Zhongshan Hall
description: The Zhongshan Tower in Yangmingshan National Park was built in the 54th year of the Republic of China (1965 AD) to commemorate the centenary of the birth of Dr. Sun Yat-sen, the founding father of the country, when President Chiang Kai-shek was in power. It was planned by the famous architect Ms. Xiu Zelan. It is located in the greenery surrounded by mountains. Its appearance is A traditional Chinese classical building with elegant and meticulous interior furnishings. It used to be the venue for the National Assembly and an important venue for heads of state to receive foreign guests or hold state banquets. Now it has been designated as a municipal historic site and is open to the public. It is a building with historical commemorative value.

name: Beitou Library
description: Beitou Library is Taiwan's first green building library. It is located in Beitou Park, next to the Beitou Hot Spring Museum, with one basement and two floors above ground. The entire building is built using environmentally friendly green energy methods. The roof is made of lightweight ecological materials and is equipped with solar photovoltaic panels to generate electricity. The green roof and sloped turf can naturally drain water to the rainwater recovery tank, which can then be recycled for watering plants and flushing toilets. It not only greens the entire library and reduces water waste. In the 101st year of the Republic of China (2012 AD), it was selected as one of the "25 Most Beautiful Public Libraries in the World" by the American website Flavorwire.com.

name: Taipei Municipal Children's New Paradise
description: Taipei Municipal Children's New Paradise (hereinafter referred to as Children's New Paradise) was formerly the Taipei Municipal Children's Education Center in Yuanshan. On April 11, 2006, the entire Children's Education Center was included in the scope of the national heritage site. Due to its geographical location, it is subject to many restrictions such as navigation heights, the Cultural Assets Preservation Law, and the Water Conservancy Law. The development, renewal, and operation of the original site have been greatly affected and restricted.

name: Yangmingshan Hot Spring Area - Xiaoyoukeng
description: Yangmingshan Hot Spring is located in the Datun volcanic zone. Volcanic action produces geothermal heat and is rich in hot spring resources. The hot spring quality is mainly white sulfur spring, followed by green sulfur spring. It is one of the four major hot springs in Taiwan along with Beitou Hot Spring, Guanziling Hot Spring and Sichongxi Hot Spring. The hot spring area is divided into front mountain hot spring and back mountain hot spring. There are many hot spring resort hotels in the surrounding area. The rich natural ecology and geological landscape, plus mountain game delicacies, make it a good place for vacation in the north.

name: Light Spot Taipei
description: The location of Light Point Taipei is a historical witness to the diplomatic relations between China and the United States. This building once served as the U.S. Consulate, Consulate General and Embassy in Taipei. After the U.S. Embassy in Taipei was officially closed in 1979, the building was abandoned for many years. In 1997, it was officially designated as a third-level historic site (now a municipality designated historic site). It reopened under the name "Taipei House" in November of the 1990s of the Republic of China (2002 AD). The exterior of this building is a white two-story Western-style building. The interior is laid out with a central corridor and stairwell. The columns are simple Greek columns. It is an art and cultural space focusing on film culture, integrating traces and movies. It houses an exhibition hall, an art hall, a small cinema, a light food restaurant and a bookstore with the theme of "movie" and "city".

name: Beitou Hot Spring Museum
description: The Beitou Hot Spring Museum was formerly known as the "Beitou Public Baths". It was planned under the order of Imura Daiyoshi, the director of Taipei during the Japanese colonial period, and supervised by Moriyama Matsunosuke, the architect of the Governor's Office. It was completed on June 17, 1913 (the second year of Taisho). It is a two-story building with a Japanese and Western eclectic style. It was also the largest hot spring public bath in East Asia at that time. The bath area on the first floor is made of brick, the rest area on the second floor is made of wood, and the entrance is on the second floor. The bathhouse was built using public health funds from the Taipei State Department at the time and modeled on the Izuyama Hot Spring Bathhouse in Shizuoka Prefecture, Japan. The rest area on the second floor is equipped with a pavilion, a shoe-changing entrance, and a tatami hall where visitors can cool off after taking a bath. There is also a protruding platform "watchtower" next to the hall, where you can enjoy the scenery of Beitou's mountains and waters. In addition, meals and drinks are sold indoors, and sometimes artistic performances are even arranged. In 1923 (the 12th year of Taisho), the Japanese Crown Prince Hirohito came to Taiwan for inspection. He also visited Beitou’s public baths and inspected Beitou stones in the stream. For this reason, the bathhouse also built an "Imperial Rest Room" on the second floor for them to rest, which is located in the audio-visual room of the current Wenzhou Museum.

name: National Photography and Cultural Center Taipei Branch
description: The "National Photography Cultural Center" is located at the intersection of Zhongxiao West Road and Huaining Street, Zhongzheng District, Taipei City. This building was formerly the "Osaka Merchant Shipping Co., Ltd. Taipei Branch" completed in 1937. The building's facade is in a simple modernist style, and a traditional oriental-style tower with a spire is built at the corner of the roof, reflecting the "Xingya-style" architectural style of the 1930s. After the Second World War, the Taiwan Aviation Industry Co., Ltd. and the Taiwan Provincial Highway Bureau (the predecessor of the Highway Administration of the Ministry of Transportation) were located here. In 2014, it was designated as a municipal historic site by the Taipei City Cultural Affairs Bureau, and the Ministry of Culture designated this historic site to be restored and reused as the base site of the "National Photography Cultural Center". After opening in 2021, the Taipei Pavilion will serve as a venue for photography and video art exhibitions, exchanges, and educational promotions, giving new life to the cultural value of historic sites.

name: Taiwan Contemporary Culture Experimental Site
description: Taiwan's Contemporary Culture Laboratory (C-LAB) has been launched in 2018. It was formerly the Industrial Research Institute of the Taiwan Governor-General's Office during the Japanese occupation. In 1949, it was changed to the Air Force Headquarters of the Republic of China. The old office building, war situation building and 15 buildings in the park (former historical and auxiliary facilities) in the base were declared as national historic sites by the Ministry of Culture in 2024. Nowadays, C-LAB is gradually revitalizing the field, opening up the participation and entry of the public, arts and cultural professionals, technology teams, and animation industries. Through cross-field and cross-disciplinary collaboration and co-creation, C-LAB launches a variety of exhibition activities and public promotion plans, and expands the spirit and practice of cultural experimentation through the innovative energy of art and culture.

name: Xikou (Rainbow) Pier
description: During the Qianlong period, the Songshan area was named "Xikou" in ancient times. Xikou Ferry, located at the water gate of No. 4 Songhe Street, has been a place for north-south trade and goods distribution since ancient times. It was once prosperous and the starting port for the development of Xikou culture in Songshan area. In 1998, in order to extend the blue highway route, the Taipei City Government completed the construction of the Xikou Pier on December 15, renovated the surrounding bank protection and the overall landscape of the waterfront walk, and connected the pedestrian walkway between the Xikou Pier and the Evacuation Gate No. 4. Moreover, Xikou Wharf is close to the Rainbow Bridge, Songshan Ciyou Palace, Raohe Tourist Night Market and other special attractions. It will become another tourist landmark in your mind if you have food and fun.

name: Taipei World Trade Center
description: At the intersection of Keelung Road and Xinyi Road, there is a pink building in District 1, which is divided into four buildings with four major functions, namely the current exhibition building, international trade building, international conference center and Grand Hyatt Hotel. More than 70 exhibitions are held here every year, attracting millions of visitors.

name: Guanghua Digital New World
description: Guanghua Mall opened in 1973 under the Guanghua Bridge between Bade Road and Citizen Avenue in Taipei City. Its original stores were old bookstalls that moved from Guling Street, and unlicensed stalls that moved in from the Bade Road area. Due to the limited number of items sold in the early stage, the mall's business did not improve much at first.

name: Beitou Park
description: "Beitou" always has endless humanities, legends and stories for people to tell. After getting off the Xinbeitou MRT station, following the curls of hot spring smoke, in front of you is the green and beautiful scenery of the hot spring town, which is Beitou Park. Beitou Park consists of Beitou 1, 2, 4, 54, and 55 urban planning parks, covering an area of ​​61,129 square meters. The first thing that catches the eye is the entrance spring that was completed in 1998. It has lights and water springs dancing with music at fixed times every day, reinjecting a new vitality into Beitou, an old Taipei area with rich culture. Along the side of Guangming Road, passing by rare old trees such as paperbark alba and Luhua tree, witness the richness of Beitou Park, which is about to turn 100 years old. history, during the journey, you will also pass by the Green Library, which was first built by the Taipei Municipal Library. It emphasizes energy conservation and carbon saving, and also brings a bookish atmosphere to Beitou Park. The fountain at the entrance is the first choice for movie shooting. Walk along the Beitou Creek. The only "Beitou Stone" in the world named after a place in Taiwan was produced here, although it is no longer seen. Cross the path and go up the stairs to the side of Zhongshan Road. In addition to the Beitou open-air hot spring bath, there is also the "Plum Garden" historical building named by Mr. Yu Youren. It has been planned by the Taipei City Government Tourism and Communications Bureau as the Plum Garden Visitor Center to provide tourists with the most considerate services. There is the famous hot spring museum, which combines Japanese and Western wooden window lattice and red brick building. It seems to be filled with the unique fragrance of sulfur. Feel the beauty of the architecture during the Japanese occupation. The surrounding gurgling streams and swaying green scenery make you feel like you have returned to the old days. Beitou Park has endless old stories and a variety of animals and plants. It is also surrounded by famous attractions such as the Geothermal Valley. You might as well take advantage of the holiday to arrange an intellectual trip to cleanse your body and mind. I believe you will return with a full load. Park location: Beitou Park 1: Next to No. 2, Zhongshan Road, Taipei City Beitou Park 2: No. 4-1, Zhongshan Road, Taipei City Beitou Park 3: No. 5-7, Zhongshan Road, Taipei City Beitou Park 4: Opposite to No. 227, Guangming Road, Taipei City Beitou Park 5: Opposite to No. 283, Guangming Road, Taipei City Management unit: Yangmingshan Park Management Office Contact number: 2883-2130

name: 140 Highland Park
description: 140 Highland Park covers an area of 5.6 hectares. It is located in Wanmeili, Wenshan District, Taipei City, on the north side of Wanning Street, on the hilly land between Wanning Street and Wanmei Street Section 2. The highest altitude of 138 meters is the Zouzijiao Mountain, which is located in 140 Highland Park next to Wanning Street. Before Wanfang Community existed, the park land was called Baozijiao. The vast hilly land where 45 families live is now located at the foot of Baozaijiao Mountain at an altitude of 138 meters, with a vast view from the top. Wenshan (Muzha) Park No. 80 (an area of about 2.2 hectares) was built in 1993, and Wenshan (Muzha) Park No. 30 (an area of about 3.4 hectares) was built in 1996. The two are nicknamed "140 Highland Park". The park's trailhead is located next to No. 125 and No. 225 Wanning Street. Go up the winding wooden stairs. After climbing the ridge, it turns into a gravel staircase trail. Follow the ridge and enjoy the rich forest. There are viewing platforms and pavilions along the way. The view is excellent. You can overlook the landscape down the mountain, overlooking the 101 Building and the lights of Wanjia, and overlooking the mountains and waters of Wenshan District. It is the best place to watch the stars and the moon. In order to create a sustainable ecological environment, the original landform was maintained as much as possible when the park was opened to avoid destroying the habitats of animals and plants. Only necessary facilities and trails were installed in the park to connect the surrounding green spaces, providing citizens with a natural place for exercise and rest. Local people built a concrete pool at their own expense in Lane 23, Wanning Street. They used the original power system and set up a simple filter tank to filter the pool water. The pool is about 100 centimeters deep. To maintain the safety of tourists and the overall landscape, the original pool walls were removed and replaced with piles of stones to surround the pool. It was completed in March 1996. It has successfully attracted frogs to inhabit it, and the frogs chirp loudly, making it more peaceful. This park also has the only "mountain sign guide map" in Taipei City, where you can learn about the mountains and their names and heights. There are also simple fitness facilities, sports equipment, stretching chairs, etc. While hiking and admiring the scenery, you can also experience the joy of stretching your muscles and bones in the quiet mountains. (Source: Taipei City Government Works Bureau Park Street Light Engineering Management Office)

name: Taipei Tianhou Temple
description: Taipei Tianhou Temple, commonly known as "Ximending Mazu Temple", together with Menga Longshan Temple and Menga Patriarch Temple, were known as the three major temples in Taiwan during the Qing Dynasty. As soon as you step into the temple gate, the noisy pop music and loud voices in your ears disappear instantly, replaced by the lingering scent of sandalwood and a solemn and peaceful atmosphere. The unique feature of this temple is that it is the only place in Taiwan where "Taiwanese and Japanese gods and Buddhas are worshiped together". The main hall is dedicated to Mazu, the merciful heavenly Virgin Mother, who protects tourists and merchants. The side hall is dedicated to Kobo Daishi, the founder of the Japanese Shingon sect. Every year, monks from Mount Koya, Japan come here to hold Dharma ceremonies, and it also attracts countless Japanese tourists to come for pilgrimage. In addition, the temple has thoughtfully set up a small area with tables, chairs and restrooms in the hall, so that tourists who are tired of shopping in Ximending or have urgent needs can take a break and tidy up here. You might as well visit the shops around Chengdu Road after praying for blessings and getting some respite.

name: Windward Riverside Park
description: It is located between Dazhi Bridge on the Keelung River and Zhongshan Expressway, covering an area of ​​approximately 273,387 square meters. The biggest feature of the park is the "Windward Dog Sports Park" specially designed for dogs. It covers an area of ​​about 1 hectare and is divided into big dog area and small dog area based on the weight of 9 kilograms. Stainless steel fences and double doors are installed as human and dog protection measures. There are also dog toilet cleaning facilities, as well as 8 resting seats and 4 foot-washing stations, so that the owners can wash their hands and the dogs can wash their feet after playing. The waterfront lawn on the river bank is a great place for families to gather, play and rest. The sports field is another feature of Windward Riverside Park. There are many facilities for people to show off their skills and exercise, including badminton, baseball and softball, football, inline skating driving ranges and other sports facilities. In addition, there is also a super mini golf driving range!

name: Dajia Riverside Park
description: Dajia Riverside Park is located between Zhongshan Bridge and Dazhi Bridge in Zhongshan District. It is an urban green park developed and constructed by the municipal government after the Keelung River was straightened. It has a large area. When you enter the park, you will see a vast endless grass garden, and you can also look at the Miramar Ferris wheel in the distance. The scenery is beautiful. There are five major game areas and bicycle rental areas in the park, all with different characteristics. The double-track zipline area is equipped with single-point and seat-type ziplines, allowing children to experience different fun; the integrated sandpit area has slides, climbing facilities, sandpits, and a shade area for parents to rest; the hill slide game area has 8 grindstone slides, climbing nets and ropes, so you don’t have to worry about not being able to play with the slide; the swing and octopus and dolphin scenic area have 5 special swings. There are also various play equipment such as a large octopus landscape, a balance beam, and a spherical hiding area. The children's water area is open from June to September every year. It is equipped with water spray facilities such as large circles, columns, and giant flowers. It is cute and fun. There is also a large water spray feature with a central water column as high as 75 meters. The visual changes in the height and intensity of the water feature are used to show its rhythmic characteristics. There is also a sports park in the park, with basketball, net, badminton, croquet and other sports facilities, as well as several kilometers of bicycle paths surrounding the park (bike rentals are available in the park). Due to its wide space, convenient parking, and beautiful environment, Dajia Riverside Park not only has many people playing and exercising here during holidays, but also holds various large-scale activities from time to time, showing the vibrant side of Taipei City.

name: Fuzhou Mountain Park
description: The Park Department took over Fuzhou Mountain Park in 1990, and compiled a budget in 1993 to dismantle the ground features. After successively removing the ground features, it was greened and beautified in a way that maintained the original style. It also built a pavilion based on the opinions of mountain friends to integrate with the original park, giving Taipei citizens a new place to wear and a better place to relax. The park is located on the hillside next to Xinhai Road and Wolong Street. It covers an area of approximately 172,488 square meters and is approximately 105 meters above sea level. It was originally the Fuzhou Mountain Cemetery. Since the park was established, the planning has focused on natural ecological conservation, with extensive planting of trees. The forest is complete, the ecology is rich, and the scenery is pleasant. In addition to necessary soil and water conservation and In addition to the disaster prevention facilities, the rest of the man-made facilities are based on the principle of minimization and easy management and maintenance. Hiking trails are set up along the way. Along the way, insects and birds chirp, the air is fresh, and pavilions are set up for rest. You can overlook Guanyin Mountain and Datun Mountain, and have a bird's eye view of the Da'an District cityscape. It is also the best place to view the whole view of 101. It is truly a paradise of tranquility in the bustle. The planting plan is based on the principle of preserving the natural features of the park. Only the entrances to the hiking trails, resting platforms and pavilions are planted with shade, bird and butterfly attracting trees, flowering trees, shrubs, etc. The former cemetery has now become a garden frequently visited by hikers and a good place for ecological teaching. (Source: Taipei City Government Works Bureau Park Access website)

description: Located in Tianmu, where expats gather, Shidong Market displays a harmonious and exquisite market style. In addition to selling fresh fruits and vegetables and fresh meat, there is a well-known nigiri sushi restaurant on the first floor that you can eat standing up, and a traditional food stall on the second floor, which is famous for its ordinary delicious taste. There are also shops selling a variety of rice, and the prices are cheaper than department stores. The items sold at Shidong Market are of a certain quality, and the interior is clean. There is no humidity or fishy smell like ordinary traditional markets. In addition, there is an underground parking lot. It is a good place to buy ingredients in the north where it often rains. It also has a warm atmosphere. You can feel the unique flavor of Taipei city, and it also reflects the daily life of the locals.

name: Taipei underground shopping mall
description: Taipei Underground Street is located in Zhongzheng District, Taipei City. It is an important part of the Taipei Station underground street system. It connects Taipei Main Station, Taipei MRT and surrounding business districts. It is one of the sizable underground streets in Taiwan. As the transportation hub of Taipei City, it is not only a must-stop for tourists, but also a multi-functional place integrating shopping, leisure and entertainment, which is very popular among tourists. There are a wide variety of shops in the underground street, covering a variety of products such as fashion clothing, electronic products, cultural and creative products, handicrafts, etc. For animation fans, Taipei Underground Mall is a must-visit destination. It has many animation peripheral stores, attracting a large number of fans to come looking for precious collectibles or the latest animation peripheral products. Every August, the "Yukata Festival" is held in Taipei's underground shopping malls, bringing a strong Japanese flavor. The venue is specially decorated with a Japanese theme scene, allowing visitors to experience the fun of wearing a yukata. There are also various Japanese elements for taking photos and checking in, making it one of the most popular activities in summer. In addition to shopping, Taipei underground shopping malls also have a wealth of entertainment facilities, including game consoles and gashapon machines, making them an ideal place for families and children to travel together.

name: Dungan Park
description: Dun'an Park was established in the 70s of the Republic of China and renovated in the 90s of the Republic of China. Located in Dunhuang Lane, Da'an District, the park covers an area of ​​2,820 square meters. Dun'an Park is surrounded by residential areas, and there is a Zhengsheng children's talent class and a seedling kindergarten. In the morning, the park has morning clubs such as aerobics and aerobic rhythmic gymnastics. In the afternoon, children in the nearby kindergarten have a high usage rate. In addition to good-neighbor mutual aid and social activities, the Dunhuang Lane office also organizes various activities in the park from time to time based on community resources. There is a majestic pavilion in the park, which is the finishing touch of Dun'an Park. In addition, the stone sculptures along the park paths also give the park a quaint artistic conception. The dense trees on the skating rink and children's play area provide the best shade for residents who are active here. Such a comfortable and beautiful activity space turns the park into a lively place for recreation and walking in the afternoon. Recreational facilities: pavilion. Recreational facilities: rockers, slides, swings, climbing frames. Sports facilities: uneven bars, ice rink. (Source: Taipei City Government Civil Affairs Bureau)
